targetTexts.1: After this, Job opened his mouth and cursed the day of his birth.
targetTexts.2: And this is what he said:
targetTexts.3: “May the day of my birth perish, and the night it was said, ‘A boy is conceived.’
targetTexts.4: If only that day had turned to darkness! May God above disregard it; may no light shine upon it.
targetTexts.5: May darkness and gloom reclaim it, and a cloud settle over it; may the blackness of the day overwhelm it.
targetTexts.6: If only darkness had taken that night away! May it not appear among the days of the year; may it never be entered in any of the months.
targetTexts.7: Behold, may that night be barren; may no joyful voice come into it.
targetTexts.8: May it be cursed by those who curse the day—those prepared to rouse Leviathan.
targetTexts.9: May its morning stars grow dark; may it wait in vain for daylight; may it not see the breaking of dawn.
targetTexts.10: For that night did not shut the doors of the womb to hide the sorrow from my eyes.
targetTexts.11: Why did I not perish at birth; why did I not die as I came from the womb?
targetTexts.12: Why were there knees to receive me, and breasts that I should be nursed?
targetTexts.13: For now I would be lying down in peace; I would be asleep and at rest
targetTexts.14: with kings and counselors of the earth, who built for themselves cities now in ruins,
targetTexts.15: or with princes who had gold, who filled their houses with silver.
targetTexts.16: Or why was I not hidden like a stillborn child, like an infant who never sees daylight?
targetTexts.17: There the wicked cease from raging, and there the weary find rest.
targetTexts.18: The captives enjoy their ease; they do not hear the voice of the oppressor.
targetTexts.19: Both small and great are there, and the slave is freed from his master.
targetTexts.20: Why is light given to the miserable, and life to the bitter of soul,
targetTexts.21: who long for death that does not come, and search for it like hidden treasure,
targetTexts.22: who rejoice and greatly exult when they reach the grave?
targetTexts.23: Why is life given to a man whose way is hidden, whom God has hedged in?
targetTexts.24: I sigh when food is put before me, and my groans pour out like water.
targetTexts.25: For the thing I feared has overtaken me, and what I dreaded has befallen me.
targetTexts.26: I am not at ease or quiet; I have no rest, for trouble has come.”
